## How to use this starter

unfinished starter can render. Replace each TODO, remove that option, and render
again. A successful render of the untouched starter is not completion.

## Supplied synthetic data and helpers

```{r}
# Simulate one two-arm trial. Returns a data frame with `arm` and `y`.
# Control is N(0, sd_ctrl^2); treatment is N(delta, sd_trt^2).
simulate_trial <- function(n_ctrl, n_trt, sd_ctrl, sd_trt, delta = 0) {
  stopifnot(n_ctrl >= 2, n_trt >= 2, sd_ctrl > 0, sd_trt > 0)

  data.frame(
    arm = rep(c("ctrl", "trt"), c(n_ctrl, n_trt)),
    y   = c(rnorm(n_ctrl, mean = 0,     sd = sd_ctrl),
            rnorm(n_trt,  mean = delta, sd = sd_trt))
  )
}

set.seed(6301)
head(simulate_trial(3, 3, 12, 4, delta = 8), 3)

analyse_trial <- function(data, pooled = FALSE) {
  x <- data$y[data$arm == "trt"]
  y <- data$y[data$arm == "ctrl"]
  fit <- t.test(x, y, var.equal = pooled)
  c(est = mean(x) - mean(y), se = fit$stderr,
    p = fit$p.value, lo = fit$conf.int[1], hi = fit$conf.int[2])
}
set.seed(6301)
round(analyse_trial(simulate_trial(20, 20, 12, 4, delta = 8)), 3)

draw_error <- function(n, target_sd, dgm = "normal") {
  if (dgm == "normal") return(rnorm(n, 0, target_sd))
  if (dgm != "skewed") stop("unknown dgm")
  a <- 0.7
  mu <- exp(a^2 / 2)
  sigma <- sqrt((exp(a^2) - 1) * exp(a^2))
  target_sd * (rlnorm(n, 0, a) - mu) / sigma
}

simulate_dgm <- function(n_ctrl, n_trt, sd_ctrl, sd_trt,
                         delta = 0, dgm = "normal") {
  data.frame(arm = rep(c("ctrl", "trt"), c(n_ctrl, n_trt)),
    y = c(draw_error(n_ctrl, sd_ctrl, dgm),
          delta + draw_error(n_trt, sd_trt, dgm)))
}
set.seed(1403)
head(simulate_dgm(10, 40, 12, 4, 6, "skewed"), 3)

analyse_checked <- function(data, pooled = FALSE) {
  tryCatch({
    value <- analyse_trial(data, pooled)
    if (any(!is.finite(value))) stop("nonfinite result")
    list(value = value, error = NA_character_)
  }, error = function(e) list(value = NULL, error = conditionMessage(e)))
}
bad_data <- data.frame(arm = rep(c("ctrl", "trt"), each = 3), y = 1)
analyse_checked(bad_data)$error
```

## 3. Retain each method and replicate

Inspect the supplied run_study(s, B) function and run a pilot with B = 5. Identify where it generates one dataset, applies both methods, and retains results or errors. Check that five replicates produce ten rows. Both methods must use the same dataset in each replicate.

```{r}
run_study <- function(s, B) {
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1L, length(B) == 1L, is.finite(B), B >= 2, B == as.integer(B))
  rows <- vector("list", 2L * B)
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    d <- simulate_dgm(s$n_ctrl, s$n_trt, 12, 4, s$delta, s$dgm)
    for (j in 1:2) {
      ans <- analyse_checked(d, pooled = j == 2L)
      value <- if (is.null(ans$value)) setNames(rep(NA_real_, 5),
        c("est", "se", "p", "lo", "hi")) else ans$value
      rows[[2L * (b - 1L) + j]] <- data.frame(
        scenario = s$scenario, replicate = b, method = c("Welch", "pooled")[j],
        n_ctrl = s$n_ctrl, n_trt = s$n_trt, delta = s$delta, dgm = s$dgm,
        as.list(value), error = ans$error)
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
```


## Optional extensions

- Add `dgm = "skewed"` to the design using the supplied helper. Explain why it centers errors using the population mean rather than each sample mean. Keep the estimand unchanged.
- Report empirical SE, mean model SE, RMSE, mean interval width, and MCSE for bias or coverage.
- Plan B from a target MCSE using `ceiling(p * (1 - p) / target^2)`. Try B = 4000 and explain why MCSE is about half its value at B = 1000.
- Explore `SimDesign::runSimulation()` for running a larger study or `rsimsum::simsum()` for summarising saved results. No package installation is required for the core lab.
